asks: Does a fork carry the sign-in of an agent program?
answer: No. A fork is made without the sign-ins that agent programs keep on the disk, as it is made without secrets, unless you, or a rule you set, let it carry one. In a fork without one, you sign in again. Silo can leave out only the sign-in of a program it knows: for another, the fork may carry it, and Silo says so before the fork is made.
